This is a personal opinion type thing and i would like discussion.

I have an idea of what a combat or fighting pistol should. Basically i see it as a double stack 9mm, 40sw or .45acp with 4" or more barrel designed with useability and reliablity in mind. it or an approximate variant can be had over the shelf. lastly, it is a pistol YOU will not second guess if mortal combat begins with you involved. (my preference include Glock 17/19, original XD 40, sig 228/229)

what is a combat pistol to you? which is more in line with your philosophy of combat pistols, striker fired or hammer fired?

I think the answer is different for everyone. I'm comfortable with the answer I've come up with, but my priorities won't necessarily match with anyone else's.

A SD pistol, first and foremost, need to be available when you require it. Bigger, heavier, thicker guns get carried less, and you have to be honest about how much effort you will actually put in to lugging it around, every single day. A smaller pistol that's always there is unquestionably the better choice if the bigger gun is left at home.

Once you've passed that hurdle and have limited yourself to the set of reliable guns that you actually will carry, I think Cooper's categorization of Accuracy/Power/Speed will help determine the best choice. Measure yourself on a scale of 1 to 3 in each of those categories - at seven yards, are you hitting a playing card, a paper plate, a barn door? Are you shooting a .380, a 9mm, a .357? Can you draw and score your first hit in 2 seconds, 4 seconds, 6 seconds? The lowest of your three scores is your total score.

Of course it gets more complicated than that. For example, what exactly do we mean by speed? A very small gun that can be kept in a jacket pocket - and actually gripped as a threat develops, without anyone else knowing - is incredibly fast, assuming you have that warning first. That same gun might as well be on Mars if you are knocked down and wrestling with someone before you know you're in danger. The gun behind your hip - and perhaps under your jacket - is often unreachable when you are belted into your car seat. You have to factor this stuff into your thinking, and make what adjustments you can. There is no one perfect answer.

Once we've been honest about what we'll really carry, and what we can really hit quickly with, then the last step is to be honest about our level of skill and our emotional response to a fight. I am a fat, chronically ill old man, and my brain turns to mush when I'm under pressure. I haven't thrown a punch in anger since third grade and I am exactly as tactical as a bowl of oatmeal. I honestly expect my IQ to drop about 20 points if I'm ever in a real fight, and my days of training regularly are long behind me.

My primary defensive pistol is a DAO Sig P250 subcompact in .40 S&W. It's basically a windex bottle that shoots bullets. There is no safety, no decocker, no transition from single to double action, and that long smooth trigger will forgive me if my trigger discipline lapses a bit under pressure. I won't be double-tapping anything with any speed, but I can't do that anyway no matter what pistol you give me. What I can do is make a pretty big hole in something close, reasonably fast, even after I go full Ghostbuster and find myself terrified beyond the capacity for rational thought.

I know my limits and that's how I've adjusted to them.

My secondary gun is a KelTec P3AT that works great; I'd have replaced it with a Ruger LCP if it has ever failed me but it never has. It's not easy to shoot well but it's very easy to carry, and it works in exactly the same windex-bottle way.

I'd like to add that I live in an place where a regular carry permit is unavailable. Unless I'm traveling, which is rare these days, my carry happens only on my own property now, which is where I spent almost all my time. This greatly simplifies a lot of the choices involved. However, if the local law ever changes (and it might) I don't think I'd be doing anything different than I'm doing now, other than carrying one of these pistols all day, every day.
